slot.brief: Evaluate statements on aliphatic vs aromatic amine basicity in gas/aqueous phases and pick correct ones.

stem:
Consider the following statements about amine basicity:

I. In the gas phase, dimethylamine has a greater proton affinity than methylamine.
II. In aqueous solution, $p$-toluidine is less basic than aniline because the methyl group withdraws electrons.
III. In aqueous solution, benzylamine is more basic than aniline because its nitrogen lone pair is not conjugated with the benzene ring.

Which statements are correct?

verdicts.working: I is true: dimethylamine has greater gas-phase proton affinity than methylamine. II is false: the para-methyl group donates electron density, making p-toluidine more basic than aniline. III is true: benzylamine’s lone pair is not conjugated with the ring, so it is more basic than aniline in water.

working:
I. The additional methyl group has a $+I$ effect: $\text{PA}((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}) > \text{PA}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)$.
II. Methyl is electron-releasing; $p$-toluidine is more basic than aniline.
III. Benzylamine's nitrogen lone pair is not conjugated with the ring; aniline's is delocalised.
Correct: I and III.
